dimensions.name: max_depth
dimensions.meaning: maximum tree depth; values are log-spaced

dimensions.name: max_features
dimensions.meaning: exponent e: each split tries round(n_features ** e) features (0 = one feature, 1 = all)

dimensions.name: min_samples_leaf
dimensions.meaning: minimum number of samples per leaf

dimensions.name: min_samples_split
dimensions.meaning: minimum number of samples required to split a node; values are log-spaced

beliefs.note: General RF tuning knowledge suggests shallow trees with high regularization (large min_samples_split) and minimal feature subsampling often generalize best on small, noisy tabular datasets to avoid overfitting.
On small datasets (<1k rows), deeper trees tend to overfit; shallower is generally safer.
Higher min_samples_split enforces stronger regularization, beneficial for small sample sizes.

trust.notes: Based on general domain heuristics for random forests on small, imbalanced tabular data. Specific dataset characteristics (feature noise, signal strength) could shift the optimum.
